sop_title: FCC Government Purchase Card Program Directive (excerpt: Sections 6.A–8 and 11.B–14)
summary: This directive excerpt sets out the FCC purchase card lifecycle: nominating, training, and issuing cards; pre-authorized purchasing; monthly Statement of Account (SOA) reconciliation and certification; disputes, audits, non-compliance actions, lost cards, limit changes, and account closure on transfer or separation. Cardholders and their Approving Officials (AOs) run it, with the Agency Program Coordinator (APC), FOC RDG/TOG, the CFO, Bureau/Office Chiefs, EAC, Human Resources, and the contractor bank handling issuance, oversight, payment, and review.

sections.title: General
sections.reason: Items 1–12 (eligibility, nomination form, training, inactive accounts, tax exemption, terms and conditions, price, shipping, mandatory sources) can be reordered without losing meaning; the gating rules in items 1–5, 7–9, and 12 were mapped as steps, decisions, and exceptions.

sections.title: Single Transaction Limits and Monthly Credit Limits
sections.reason: These limit statements are reorderable; the STL gate became decision D5, EAC limit-setting became D3/S9, and the limit-increase request became S57–S59.

sections.title: Reconciliation of Statements of Accounts
sections.reason: Order matters: the receiving employee signs before the cardholder reconciles, and the cardholder signs and forwards before the AO reviews, signs, and forwards to FOC.

sections.title: Records Retention
sections.reason: The list of required documents can be reordered; the retention action (S37), the IT-hardware approval implication (S21), and the missing-documentation consequence (D16/S44) were mapped.

sections.title: Cardholder Review
sections.reason: Order matters: a reviewer or auditor requests documentation before the cardholder furnishes it directly.

sections.title: Responsibilities – Managing Director
sections.reason: States agency-level authority only and gives no action with a position in the flow.

sections.title: Responsibilities – Chief Financial Officer (CFO)
sections.reason: These responsibilities are reorderable, but data entry and bank payment are tied to receipt of reconciled SOAs, so they were mapped as S35–S36.

sections.title: Responsibilities – Bureau and Office Chiefs
sections.reason: Items 1–9 are reorderable; items 1 (nominating), 6 (timely SOA flow), 8 (disciplinary action), and 9 (status changes) are tied to points in the flow and were mapped.

sections.title: Responsibilities – Agency Program Coordinator (APC)
sections.reason: These duties are reorderable; issuing cards and opening and closing accounts tie to issuance (S10) and separation (S62), while liaison and monitoring duties have no flow position.

sections.title: Responsibilities – Approving Official (AO)
sections.reason: Items 1–9 are reorderable; items 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, and 8 are tied to flow points (before purchase, receipt, within 10 workdays, a cardholder leaving) and were mapped, while items 5 and 9 were left out.

sections.title: Responsibilities – Cardholder
sections.reason: Items 1–12 are reorderable; items tied to flow points (once nominated, before purchase, within 7 workdays, lost card, before reassignment, upon leaving) were mapped.

sections.title: Span of Control for Agency Program Coordinators and Approving Officials
sections.reason: This is a single internal-control requirement with no position in the flow.

sections.title: (Heading not visible; text begins mid-paragraph because pages covering Sections 9–11.A were not provided)
sections.reason: This is a reorderable statement of consequences for non-compliance; the APC suspension, reporting, restoration, and permanent closure actions were mapped as S45–S48.

sections.title: Criminal, Disciplinary, and Adverse Actions
sections.reason: This is a reorderable list of penalties; only the permanent-closure consequence for misuse or fraud was used, in D17/S48.

sections.title: (No heading) Personal liability for intentional misuse
sections.reason: This is a reorderable statement of liability and penalties with no actionable step.

sections.title: (No heading) APC reporting of misuse or fraud
sections.reason: Order matters: the APC reports misuse or fraud first, and any proposed disciplinary or adverse action then proceeds through Human Resources.

sections.title: Disputing a Charge – transaction disputes and steps before disputing
sections.reason: Order matters: review receipts, then contact the merchant, then dispute with the bank within 90 days, then track to completion.

sections.title: Disputing a Charge – shipping charges and taxes
sections.reason: This rule gates the bank dispute step, so it was mapped as decision D15.

sections.title: Card Security
sections.reason: These safeguarding statements are reorderable; the immediate lost/stolen report was mapped as S51.

sections.title: Separation or Transfer – Cardholder
sections.reason: Order matters: prior notice to the APC, then records and card handed over before departure, then the AO annotates the final SOA if the cardholder cannot sign.

sections.title: Separation or Transfer – AO
sections.reason: Order matters: the AO departs, then the Chief designates a new AO, then the designation is sent in writing to the APC.

sections.title: Separation or Transfer – APC
sections.reason: Order matters: the APC closes the account upon being notified of the transfer or separation.

risks.description: Form A-498 passes from nominee to Bureau/Office Chief (S3) to AO (S4) and back to the nominee for signatures with no tracking. Card issuance cannot proceed until it is complete (6.A.3, 7.F.1).
Nominee details appear on Form A-498 and again on the bank card application. FOC RDG/TOG then resubmits the application to the contractor bank (S8) (7.F.1).
D2: if the signed A-498 or GSA training certificate is missing, the card may not be issued, but no next step is stated (6.A.3, 6.A.4).
Pre-purchase authorization may be a memo, note, or email (7.E.2, 7.F.4) and is not logged centrally. 6.D still requires a copy of the advance authorization in the purchase file.
D4: no next step is stated when the AO declines or does not provide written authorization.
D5: when a purchase exceeds the single transaction limit, the card is not to be used (6.B.2), but no alternative route is stated (EAC, limit increase, other procurement).

Funds availability is ensured by the cardholder alone before purchase (7.F.5), with no independent check. The AO certifies funds availability only after the fact on the SOA (6.C.4(2)). Anti-Deficiency Act exposure.

The AO validates receipt 'as applicable' and 'prior to the cardholder's receipt' (7.E.3). It is unclear when this applies and how it relates to the receiving employee's invoice signature in 6.C.3 (S27).

The cardholder may not reconcile until the receiving employee signs the invoice (6.C.3), but reconciliation is due within 7 workdays (6.C.1). Nothing says what happens if that signature is delayed or unobtainable.

The wet-signed SOA moves from cardholder to AO (S31) and from AO to FOC RDG/TOG (S34) with no tracking. Only 3 workdays separate the 7-workday cardholder deadline and the 10-workday AO deadline (6.C.1, 6.C.2).
Reconciled transaction data from the signed SOA is re-entered into the core financial accounting system (7.B).
6.C.2 sets 10 workdays for AO review but no deadline for forwarding to FOC. 7.C.6 says only 'in a timely manner as prescribed by agency purchase card policy'.
6.D requires retention for six years. 7.F.9 requires six years after final payment. The two give different start points for the retention clock.
The cardholder tracks disputes to completion (12.A), but the SOP states no next step if the bank denies the dispute. The 90-calendar-day deadline is tracked only by the cardholder.
After a lost or stolen card is reported to the bank, AO, and APC (13, 7.F.3), no next step is stated: replacement, account closure, or review of fraudulent charges.

11.B says abuse, misuse, and non-compliance may result in temporary suspension until compliance, with permanent closure only for repeated instances. 11.C says misuse or fraud will result in permanent closure. The two sections differ on the consequence of a first misuse (S45 vs S48).
'The Bureau/Office must confirm' names no role and sets no response deadline before suspension (6.A.5).
Permanent monthly limit increases are reviewed 'on a periodic basis' with no interval stated (6.B.5).
D21: a permanent monthly increase requested for a non-OMD cardholder will not be granted (6.B.4), but no response or alternative is stated.

Different sections assign departure notice to different owners. 7.F.10: the cardholder notifies the APC. 14.A: the AO or Bureau/Office Chief gives prior notice. 7.E.8: the AO directs cancellation in writing. 7.C.9: the Chief provides status changes.
14.A requires records to go to the AO promptly and before separation or transfer. 7.F.11 says upon cancellation of the account or separation.

Account closure depends entirely on notice reaching the APC (14.C), and there is no check that it happened. A card surrendered to the AO (S64) has no stated handoff to the APC, who destroys cards (7.D).
The APC alone issues and destroys cards, opens and closes accounts, grants limit increases, and suspends privileges (7.D, 6.B, 11.B, 14.C). No backup or alternate is designated.
The new AO designation is sent to the APC in writing (14.B) with no tracking. Pending authorizations and SOA reviews have no AO until it is recorded.

starter_flows.trigger: SharePoint - When an item is modified in the SOA Reconciliations list (filter: Status = 'AO Certified')
actions: Get item and attachments for the SOA record
Condition: verify AO printed name, signature date, and any initialed exception remarks are present; if missing, set Status = 'Incomplete' and email the AO
Convert the certified SOA record to PDF and copy the package to the FOC RDG/TOG library
Send email (Outlook) to the FOC RDG/TOG shared mailbox with the package link
Update item: Status = 'Submitted to FOC', SubmittedOn = utcNow()
Condition: if SubmittedOn is later than 10 workdays after billing cycle end, set LateFlag = Yes for APC reporting

starter_flows.trigger: SharePoint - When an item is created in the Purchase Authorizations list (submitted from the Power Apps request form)
actions: Get the cardholder's AO, single transaction limit, and monthly limit from the Cardholder Register list
Condition: if amount exceeds the single transaction limit, set Status = 'Exceeds STL', notify the cardholder, and stop (route undefined in SOP; process owner to define)
Condition: verify the funding document reference and the funds-availability attestation are completed
Start and wait for an approval assigned to the AO
Update item with outcome, approver name, comments, and timestamp as the written authorization record
Send email to the cardholder with the outcome; if rejected, set Status = 'Not Authorized' (next step undefined in SOP)
starter_flows.approval_step: AO approves or rejects the purchase before it is made (7.E.2, 7.F.4); the approval response is the written authorization retained per 6.D.

starter_flows.trigger: SharePoint - When an item is modified in the SOA Reconciliations list (filter: Status = 'Cardholder Certified')
actions: Get item; verify cardholder printed name, signature date, and exception remarks
Condition: for transactions flagged as accepted by another employee, verify the receiving employee's signature and date are recorded (6.C.3); if missing, return to the cardholder
Calculate the AO due date as 10 workdays after billing cycle end
Start and wait for an approval assigned to the AO, with the SOA and supporting documents linked
Send reminder emails at intervals until the AO responds; if past due, escalate to the Bureau/Office Chief (7.C.6)
On approval: record AO name, date, and exception remarks and set Status = 'AO Certified' (triggers the A29 flow); on rejection: return to the cardholder with comments
starter_flows.approval_step: AO reviews and certifies the reconciled SOA within 10 workdays after billing cycle end (6.C.2, 7.E.4); exceptions to the Certification Clause are entered as remarks with name and date (6.C.4).
